ex-E302-1.title: Cost effectiveness of lamps
ex-E302-1.question:
The information of an LED lamp, a compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) and an incandescent lamp are shown below. The three lamps have the same brightness.

LED lamp

CFL

Incandescent lamp

Power

10 W

14 W

60 W

Lifetime

15 000 hours

10 000 hours

1000 hours

Cost

$50

$40

$15

Suppose the cost of electricity is $1.1 per kW h.

(a) Which lamp is the cheapest for 1000 hours of use?

(b) Which lamp is the cheapest for 15 000 hours of use?

(c) What are the advantages of using LED lamp over the other two lamps?
ex-E302-1.answer:
(a) Cost of using LED lamp = 1.1 × 0.01 × 1000 + 50 = $61

Cost of using CFL = 1.1 × 0.014 × 1000 + 40 = $55.4

Cost of using incandescent lamp = 1.1 × 0.06 × 1000 + 15 = $81

∴ CFL is the cheapest for 1000 hours of use.

(b) Cost of using LED lamp = 1.1 × 0.01 × 15 000 + 50 = $215

Cost of using CFL = 1.1 × 0.014 × 15 000 + 2 × 40 = $311

Cost of using incandescent lamp = 1.1 × 0.06 × 15 000 + 15 × 15

= $1215

∴ LED lamp is the cheapest for 15 000 hours of use.

(c) LED lamp has a longer lifetime and a higher energy efficiency.
ex-E302-1.tips:
Tip

Remember to convert the power of lamp from W to kW.

Tip

More than one CFL and incandescent lamp are needed for 15 000 hours of use.

ex-E302-5.title: Blue light and green light
ex-E302-5.question:
Two 880-lm lamps, A and B, emit monochromatic light of 555-nm green light and 480-nm blue light respectively. The rated power of A is 40 W and that of B is 80 W.

(a) Compare the brightness of A and B. Explain briefly.

(b) Find the efficacy of each lamp.

(c) Is the green light or the blue light emitted at a higher power? Why?
ex-E302-5.answer:
(a) A and B have the same brightness, because they have the same luminous flux.

(b) Efficacy of A = 88040 = 22 lm W−1

Efficacy of B = 88080 = 11 lm W−1

(c) The blue light is emitted at a higher power. Since our eyes are less sensitive to blue light than green light, B needs to emit blue light at a higher power so that it produces the same luminous flux as A.
ex-E302-5.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E302  |  Source PDF p. 25, 26

ex-E302-6.title: Energy label on an LED lamp
ex-E302-6.question:
The energy label affixed on an LED lamp (Fig a) and the information on its package (Fig b) are shown below.

(a) What is the luminous flux of the lamp?

(b) The package indicates that this LED lamp is as bright as a 60-W GLS lamp. What is the efficacy of the 60-W GLS lamp?

(c) Among the three lamps shown on the package, which lamp is the most energy-saving one? Explain your answer.
ex-E302-6.answer:
(a) Luminous flux = efficacy × input power

= 110 × 6.5

= 715 lm

(b) Efficacy = 71560 = 11.9 lm W−1

(c) The LED lamp is the most energy-saving lamp. This is because it consumes the least amount of power to give the same luminous flux.
ex-E302-6.location: Book E3  |  Chapter E302  |  Source PDF p. 26
